title: Launch momentum gap sprint canvas
content:
Purpose: quick, execution-focused sprint canvas to close remaining gaps across the go-to-scale window. This is intentionally tactical: 2-week sprint cycles, clear owners, measurable KPI targets, and concrete fallbacks.

How to use: 1) Populate current metric baseline in "baseline KPIs" section. 2) Add up to 6 gap workstreams (columns below). 3) Assign an owner and a primary SRE/Eng partner. 4) Set a measurable success condition and a rollback/fallback threshold. 5) Weekly standup: update progress, blockers, and whether the workstream should be promoted to emergency incident.

BASELINE KPIs (current snapshot):
- P50 latency (text gen, small model): 210ms
- P95 latency (text gen, small model): 890ms
- Token cost per 1k (hosted): $0.42
- Error rate (5xx): 0.6%
- Successful canary request ratio: 98.1%
- SLA burn rate (last 72h): 0.7%
- Traffic growth projection next 7d: +35%

SPRINT DETAILS (2-week sprint)
Sprint window: 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-17
Sprint goal: Reduce P95 latency to <=700ms under expected +35% traffic and ensure canary health >=99% at 25% rollout.

Workstream A: Small-model latency tuning
- Owner: Daniel Kim (eng-serving-runtime)
- Eng partner: Riley Chen (infra)
- Tasks: kernel selector tweak (+A/B), batch size cap adjustments, kv-cache prefetch for frequent prefixes
- Success condition: P95 <=700ms on staging with 1.2x traffic replay
- Fallback: revert kernel change and enable prefix caching only; if error rate increases >0.5% over baseline, rollback
- Jira: ENG-4402
- Notes: low-risk perf change but needs thorough memory pressure check on 8-GPU pool

Workstream B: Cache warming & prefix hydrations
- Owner: Morgan Lee (product-ops)
- Eng partner: SRE oncall (oncall-2)
- Tasks: pre-populate top-200 prefixes for top 3 customers; add proactive cache warms during deploys; instrument cache hit metric per route
- Success condition: cache hit rate >= 68% for targeted routes within 30 minutes of deploy
- Fallback: fall back to dynamic KV cache with temporary increased batch window; if token cost rises >10% over baseline, stop warms
- Jira: OPS-3890

Workstream C: Canary rollout refinement and traffic shaping
- Owner: Priya Nair (product-hosted-api)
- Eng partner: Release engineering
- Tasks: implement 4-stage canary (0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> 25%) with automated smoke checks at each stage; add slow-path throttling for long-context requests; add canary budget limiter per-tenant
- Success condition: each stage passes smoke checks (error <0.2%, latency within 1.15x baseline)
- Fallback: if smoke fails at any stage, auto-rollback to previous model variant and notify ops channel #release-control
- Linked test: smoke-suite-canary-2025

Workstream D: Cost-control and quantization trial
- Owner: Asha Patel (product-ops)
- Eng partner: Applied ML (quant team)
- Tasks: run controlled experiment with int8 quantized variant for lower-tier customers; measure quality degradation on 3 prompt sets; surface token-cost delta per 1k
- Success condition: cost down >=18% with quality drop <= 3% on eval metrics
- Fallback: pause quant route if adoption leads to >5% negative NPS signals from beta customers
- Jira: ML-1743

Workstream E: Observability and playbook readiness
- Owner: Riley Chen (observability)
- Eng partner: SRE
- Tasks: ensure dashboard tiles show per-model P50/P95, per-route cost, canary pass/fail, per-tenant SLA burn; prepare pre-made runbook snippets for top-5 failure modes
- Success condition: oncall can diagnose and execute top-3 runbook steps within 12 minutes in tabletop drill
- Fallback: if drill takes >20 minutes, escalate to incident practice and add dedicated triage rota for next 2 weeks
- Linked artifact: https://confluence.redwood/internal/runbooks/launch-2025

RAG RISK MATRIX (quick view):
- Green: Workstreams A, B are on track if daily perf regression <=1.5% and no memory regressions found
- Amber: Workstream C (canary) if >2 smoke failures in last 24h or variance in latency >20% per stage
- Red: Workstream D (quant) if cost rises or customer quality complaints >3 within beta group; Workstream E if runbook incomplete or dashboards missing key metrics

Checkpoints and decision gates (by sprint day):
- Day 2: kernel A/B performance quickcheck (pass to continue)
- Day 5: cache warm instrumentation live and baseline re-taken
- Day 8: canary stage 1 -> 2 decision gate (must pass smoke and latency SLOs)
- Day 12: quantization experiment snapshot and quality eval review
- Day 14: final go/no-go: meets success conditions for at least 3/5 workstreams OR has approved fallbacks and on-call staffing for risk windows

Who to alert and when:
- #release-control for any canary stage failure
- paging: SRE primary if SLA burn rate increases >1.5% within 6h window
- Exec update: email product-leads@redwood if final decision is degrade/rollforward change

Open questions / backlog items:
- How to reconcile prefix warming with multi-tenant privacy for sensitive prefixes? (priority: medium)
- Add small-requests slow-path: should we limit to token length <64 only? (engineering cost vs benefit)
- Should Dedicated customers be excluded from reduced-precision model experiment by default? (ask sales/legal)

Meeting cadence and artifacts to produce this sprint:
- Daily 15m stand (owner updates)
- Tue deep-dive 45m (eng + product + applied ML)
- Friday 30m demo of intermediate metrics + decision log entry
- Artifacts: weekly metrics snapshot (CSV), canary smoke log (jsonl), rollforward playbook (md)

Versioning and traceability: every change to runtime or kernel must attach PR link and CI smoke-run id inside Jira ticket. Example: ENG-4402 -> PR #891 (see linked_artifacts).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep runbook short and battle-tested. Ops hates long novels during an incident.
- Prioritize visibility over perfect mitigation for first 48h after rollout.
- If small-model P95 stays stubbornly high, consider short-lived traffic-split to larger model with prefetched responses for high-frequency routes.

Post-sprint success measurement (within 7 days after sprint):
- P95 maintained <=700ms under actual traffic for 5 consecutive 12h windows
- Canary health >=99% at 25% rollout for 72h
- Token cost delta <= +5% (net neutral or reduction if quantization used)
- No P1 incidents related to this rollout in 7 days

Appendix: quick checklist (tick boxes)
- [ ] Baseline snapshot committed to metrics repo
- [ ] All owners assigned and Jira tickets created
- [ ] Runbooks drafted for top-3 failure modes
- [ ] Canary automation pipeline rehearsed on staging
- [ ] Exec summary draft ready for Monday update

End of canvas.
